newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan says not considering court application.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan says not considering court application.

text.p: Yaohan Japan Corp on Thursday said it was not considering applying to the court for an arrangement with creditors under Japanese bankruptcy laws.
Under the court procedure, companies can continue to operate while debt repayments are made to creditors in accordance with an arrangement approved by the court.
"We have not considered such a measure at all," said a company spokesman.

He also said that financial institutions remain supportive of Yaohan's restructuring efforts, under which the company aims to cut interest-bearing group debt to 90 billion yen from 164.6 billion yen over the next two years through the sale of stores, offices and a portion of its overseas assets.

The mass circulation daily Yomiuri Shimbun reported in its wire service on Thursday that Yaohan Japan is in talks with financial institutions on possible changes in the retailer's restructuring plan and that it may be forced to apply for court mediation.

The Yaohan spokesman said the company had requested in June that some of its suppliers accept a delay in payments for several months because it was unable to immediately liquidate merchandise at 16 stores it sold in May.
The recent fall in Yaohan's share price on the Tokyo stock market reflected lingering concerns about the company's outlook.

On Thursday, Yaohan was the largest percentage loser on the Tokyo bourse, falling 17 yen to 143 yen. The retailer's shares hit a record low of 133 yen in intraday trade on Wednesday before recovering to close at 160.
